problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ -3 & -5 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A,$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding an Orthogonal Basis Using the Gram-Schmidt Process
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072057/assets/1e6a41f2d6f834b7f9b8c937d19a4f47d45ee6bf2705d783e9a254e8478df15d.png)

Suppose that $V = \textrm{Span}\{\mathbf a_1, \mathbf a_2, \mathbf a_3\}.$ Given that $\mathcal B$ is an orthogonal basis for $V,$ and that $\mathcal B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\dfrac{b}{c}?$
examples.worked_solution:
We find an orthogonal basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072057/assets/3f7fd351c90e195ff46d0fdec20b2bda8a5a784c17a97700238fab0b19ebe836.png)

**Step 2.** We find the vector $\mathbf{v}_2$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1\}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{3}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector $\mathbf{v}_3$ orthogonal to $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2 \}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{3}{3})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{3}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $b=\dfrac 3 2,$ $c=-\dfrac 3 2,$ and $\dfrac{b}{c} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac 3 2\right)}{\left(-\dfrac 3 2\right)}=-1.$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{d}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{6}{4})[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{12}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(6[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+9[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{a}{d}=\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{(-\frac{2}{3})}=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$
